title: Platform systems & services - dashboards, alerts, runbooks, roadmap (Q4 2026)
author: Priya Menon
body:
Overview:
This document consolidates the platform systems & services inventory, dashboard and alerting standards, operational runbooks, recent retrospectives, and the Q4 2026 roadmap. Intended audience: Platform engineers, SRE, on-call, and engineering managers.

Quick summary:
- Primary goal: keep Redwood's inference control plane and serving surface at or above our SLOs while reducing alert noise and improving on-call resolution time.
- Core SLOs: 99.95% availability for control-plane APIs; p95 request latency < 150ms for small model routes; median model-inference token latency goals remain route-dependent and are documented per-model.

1) Systems & Services inventory (owner / primary contact):
- control-router: routes API requests, enforces rate limits - owner: platform-routing (pager: PD1)
- model-proxy: translates API calls to serving runtime requests - owner: serving-runtime (pager: PD2)
- kv-cache: prefix and KV cache for token caching - owner: serving-runtime
- batcher: request batching layer used by dedicated pools - owner: gpu-fleet
- metrics-collector (otel-collector): ingestion and forwarding to Cortex/Tempo - owner: observability
- infra-orch (terraform-state + controllers): manages infra lifecycle for Dedicated and Private - owner: infra-team
- auth-gateway (rbac/jwt): tenant auth and key validation - owner: security-infra

2) Dashboards and standard views:
All dashboards live in Grafana (dash IDs linked in runbooks). Standard dashboards and owners:
- Platform Overview (team: platform-ops) - key panels: 1) global request rate; 2) error rate by route; 3) latency p50/p95 per model; 4) queue depth for batcher.
- Serving Pool Health (gpu-fleet) - GPU utilization, OOM counts, model-evictions, kernel-fallback rates.
- Cache Effectiveness (serving-runtime) - KV hit ratio, cache evictions per minute, byte-size per keyspace.
- Control Plane Latency (platform-routing) - p50/p95/p99 control-plane API latencies, DB call latencies.
- Cost & Throughput (finance + platform) - tokens/sec, cost-per-token estimates, autoscale events.

Dashboard links (examples):
- Platform Overview: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/1001/platform-overview
- Serving Pool Health: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/1102/serving-pool-health

3) Alerting standards and thresholds (policy):
- Alert classification: P0 (page immediately), P1 (page during business hours), P2 (ticket + slack), P3 (dashboard-only).
- General thresholds (examples):
  - control-router errors: error-rate > 1% for 5m -> P0
  - control-router latency: p95 > 800ms for 10m -> P1
  - model-proxy 5xx: 5xx-rate > 0.5% for 5m -> P0 if traffic > 50rps else P1
  - GPU OOMs: any OOM on >1 node in 5m -> P1
  - KV cache hit ratio: drop 30% vs baseline for 15m -> P2
  - Prometheus scraping failures for metrics-collector: missing 3 consecutive scrapes -> P1

Alerting noise reduction rules:
- Use anomaly detection only where static thresholds generate >10 false pages/week.
- Add suppression for planned maintenance windows tied to deployment tags.
- Require runbook tags on every alert (link to runbook id).

4) Standard runbooks (links + TL;DR):
- control-router 5xx spike (runbook id: RB-PL-1001):
  1) Check Platform Overview dashboard panels (error rate, recent deploy ID).
  2) Verify recent deploys: `deployctl list --since 30m` and rollback if change correlates.
  3) Validate backend connectivity: `curl -sS https://model-proxy.internal/health`
  4) If traffic overload suspected, enable rate-limit fallback route: `rzctl set-route-fallback control-router --mode=throttle`
  5) Page PD1 and escalate to SRE manager if not resolved in 15m.
- serving-pool GPU OOMs (RB-PL-1102):
  1) Identify nodes with OOM: `kubectl get pods -o wide -l app=batcher` + check node GPU logs.
  2) If OOM due to new model: remove model allocation from affected pool and trigger graceful eviction.
  3) If OOM due to kernel regression, set kernel-fallback label and open kernel regression issue.
- metrics ingestion outage (RB-PL-1203):
  1) Check otel-collector (+logs in Loki) and Cortex ingestion health.
  2) If collector crashed, restart via `kubectl rollout restart deploy/otel-collector` and monitor.

Runbook ownership and maintenance cadence:
- Each runbook has an owner and a quarterly review date. Owners must run a tabletop once per quarter and update the runbook after any tech changes.

5) On-call and escalation matrix:
- Pager duty routing: PD1 -> platform-sre -> SRE lead; PD2 -> serving-runtime -> runtime lead.
- Escalation timeline: 0-15m incident acknowledgment, 15-45m mitigation/action, 45+m exec notify (if unresolved).
- Communication channels: #oncall-alerts for automated pages, #incidents for ongoing coordination, incident Zoom link is generated automatically by PD when a PD incident is acknowledged.

6) Retrospective highlights (recent Q3 2026 retro):
- Problem observed: increase in false-positive control-router alerts after moving to a new rate-limiting algorithm.
- Root cause: threshold tuning not updated for per-tenant burst patterns.
- Actions taken: adjusted anomaly detector baseline, added per-tenant burst exemption, wrote unit tests for new limiter behavior.
- Metrics after action: false pages/week dropped from ~36 to 6; mean time to acknowledge reduced from 9m to 4m.

7) Q4 2026 roadmap (high level):
- Improve alert precision: expand ML-based anomaly detection to 6 more dashboards (target: reduce P0 false pages by 70%).
- Cache improvements: implement multi-tenant KV sizing and eviction policies; target 20% improvement in hit ratio for small-sequence workloads.
- Observability: add distributed tracing hooks for the batcher -> model-proxy path; instrument token-level latency breakdown.
- Reliability: finish canary rollback automation for model-proxy and control-router (target: reduce rollback time to <5m).
- Runbooks & playbooks: migrate canonical runbooks to new runbook service with revisioned templates and playbook SLAs.

8) How-tos (selected):
- Add a new Grafana panel: create PR against grafana-dashboards repo, include panel JSON and test data link, request dashboard review.
- Update an alert rule: follow alert-change checklist: 1) change in staging only, 2) monitor for 48h, 3) request reviewer sign-off, 4) promote to prod during weekday morning window.
- Schedule maintenance for a Dedicated pool: create outage ticket, update alert suppression tags with `maintenance:<ticket-id>`, announce in #platform-ops 24h prior.

9) Team wiki & onboarding pointers:
- Platform playbook (starter): /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-playbook-2026-q2
- On-call checklist: /confluence/eng-platform/oncall-and-incident-response/checklists
- PagerDuty run-through guide (for new hires): /confluence/eng-platform/pagerduty-oncall-onboarding

10) Open risks and mitigations:
- Risk: model kernel regressions causing increased GPU OOMs. Mitigation: test harness for kernel combos and preflight CI that runs microbenchmarks on a small GPU pool before rollout.
- Risk: cross-tenant noisy neighbors in Dedicated pools. Mitigation: tenant-level autoscale and isolation knobs; per-tenant SLAs and admission controller quotas.

Appendix: useful commands and links:
- `deployctl list --since 30m` - recent deploys
- `rzctl set-route-fallback control-router --mode=throttle` - temporary throttle
- Grafana overview: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/1001/platform-overview
- Runbooks index: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/index
